albums.blurb: Toumani Diabaté, who died in 2024, was the world's foremost player of the kora, the 21-string West African harp-lute, born into a Malian griot family whose kora lineage is said to stretch back some seventy generations. The Mandé Variations, produced by Nick Gold for World Circuit, was his first entirely solo kora album since his 1988 debut Kaira, twenty years earlier — eight unaccompanied, largely improvised pieces recorded without overdubs, and instrumental from end to end.
albums.reception: The album was nominated for a Grammy Award, and World Circuit's release stands among the most widely praised solo kora recordings, with musicOMH's contemporary review calling it captivating from start to finish.

albums.blurb: Ctrl is SZA's debut studio album for Top Dawg Entertainment, arriving after years of delays that followed her 2014 EP Z. Its diaristic writing about insecurity, control, and twenty-something relationships, set over hazy guitar-flecked production, made it one of the defining R&B records of the late 2010s and set up 2022's SOS.
albums.reception: It debuted at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, was certified triple platinum by the RIAA in 2022, and became the first debut album by a Black woman to spend 300 weeks on the chart.

albums.blurb: Cortex was a Paris jazz-funk band led by keyboardist Alain Mion, and Troupeau Bleu is their debut, cut in just two days at Studio Damiens in July 1975 — Fender Rhodes grooves topped by Mireille Dalbray's airy, often wordless vocals. The record sold modestly and the band faded by the early 1980s, but crate-diggers turned the original pressing into a collector's holy grail, and Mion has since revived Cortex for reissues and international touring.
albums.reception: Troupeau Bleu has been sampled at least 142 times — most famously 'Huit Octobre 1971' on MF DOOM's 'One Beer' — and its reissues have sold over 10,000 copies, outstripping the roughly 7,000 copies of the original 1975 pressing.
